title: The rope of Allah
hookLine: hold fast together to the rope of Allah and don't divide (3:103)

cards: Before the Prophet ﷺ came to Medina, the city had two great Arab tribes, the Aws and the Khazraj. The reports call them kin, with a long history of feuds and revenge, ending in a battle called Bu'ath not long before.
Then both tribes became Muslim, and sat in the same rows to pray, with dead relatives between them. Today's verse was spoken into that room.

teach.b: Pickthall translates 3:103: "And hold fast, all of you together, to the cable of Allah, and do not separate." Cable, rope: the Arabic is habl, a rope you hold so you don't fall.
And all of you together is part of the command. It isn't a rope for one person to cling to alone.
The verse goes on: remember God's favor to you, how you were enemies, and He joined your hearts, and by His grace you became brothers. You were on the edge of a pit of fire, and He saved you from it.

Commentators hear the Aws and the Khazraj in it, though the verse names no one. The major tafsir works tell of a man who tried to reopen the old wound by having someone recite poems from the war days.
Tempers flared, hands went to weapons, and the Prophet came out and reminded them who they now were.
What is the rope? Commentators give several answers. Some say the Qur'an itself, and a report in Tirmidhi has the Prophet call the Book of God a rope stretched from heaven to earth.
Others say the covenant with God, or the community of believers, or sincere faith.

teach.h: HOLD FAST, AND DO NOT SEPARATE.
teach.b: These answers don't fight each other: many hands can hold one rope. And a rope doesn't make everyone stand in the same spot. People hold it at different points, some near, some far.
It only asks that you don't let go, and that you don't cut it.

how: Muslims often quote 3:103 in sermons and community gatherings as a call to unity, and many read the 'rope of Allah' as the Qur'an, the shared book that holds the community together.

games.q: you're in Medina. someone starts reciting old war poems between the Aws and the Khazraj. tempers rise. what happens in the story commentators tell?
o: the Prophet comes out and reminds them who they are now.
games.why: the Prophet reminds them of the faith that joined them, and they reconcile; commentators link the verses to this moment.

practice: Picture your own circle, family, friends, a mosque, a team at work, and somewhere in it a split, small or old: two people who don't talk, or you and someone you've drifted from.
Picture one rope you're both holding at different points, and ask what one small pull toward each other would look like: a message, a greeting, a kind word about them to someone else.

wordCard.voice: Habl, a rope you hold so you don't fall. Held by everyone together, in 3:103, with the command not to divide. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: hold the rope together. Nobody has to stand in the same spot. That's day three hundred sixty-nine.
